model_annotation: The chart presents grouped bar estimates of an outcome labeled “effect” across multiple language-family categories, with six model conditions shown per category and uncertainty indicated by error bars. The category axis runs along the horizontal direction (shown diagonally in the figure) and lists families in this left-to-right order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The value axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear scale with gridlines and tick labels at approximately 0, 10, 20, and 30 (with bars also extending below 0 into negative values), spanning roughly from about −20 up to the mid-30s. Each category contains a cluster of six adjacent bars in consistent colors matching the legend at lower right: mBERT-L1 (light blue), XLM-L1 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (pink), and XLM-B2 (red); each bar has a vertical error bar with caps. In IE-Baltic, all six bars are short and slightly below 0 (roughly around −2 to −5). In IE-Germanic, the light/dark blue bars extend further below 0 (around the high single-digit negatives), the green bars are also negative (roughly low-to-mid teens negative), and the pink/red bars are negative as well, with the pink bar appearing among the longer downward bars in that group (mid-to-high teens negative). In IE-Indic, the blue bars sit close to 0 but slightly negative (around −1 to −3), while the green and pink/red bars extend farther downward, including one of the longest negative bars in the figure (a light-green bar reaching to roughly around −20). In IE-Romance, all bars are negative and moderate in length (roughly a few units below 0 up to around −7). In IE-Slavic family and IE-other, the clusters again show negative bars of moderate size, with greens tending to be closer to 0 than the blues and pink/red in those groups (generally between about −1 and −10). In Isolate, all six bars are very close to 0 with small negative values (around −1 to −3). In Semitic, the blue and pink/red bars extend above 0 into positive values (approximately low teens up to around the high teens, with comparatively large error bars that reach into the 20s and around 30), while the green bars extend below 0 (around the high single-digit to low double-digit negatives). In Uralic, the bars are again near 0 with small negative values (roughly within a few units below 0). The categories are not shown as explicitly sorted by bar height (they appear in a fixed family order), and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the standard coloring and error bars.
